title: The believers' du'a
hookLine: our Lord, don't let our hearts swerve, and give us mercy from You (3:8)
tomorrow: Year two close: the book read through

cards: Umm Salamah, one of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, noticed something. A prayer he said more than any other, she reported, was this: O turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion.
She asked him why that one, so often. He answered, in the hadith recorded by at-Tirmidhi, that every human heart lies between two of the fingers of Allah, and He turns it as He wills.
The Prophet himself, asking again and again for his own heart to be kept.

teach.b: The Qur'an puts a request very like it in the mouths of a whole group. Surah three, verse seven, talks about the book itself: some verses are clear and plain, others open to more than one reading.
Some people chase the unclear ones to stir up trouble, it says.

teach.h: THE FIRMLY GROUNDED SAY: ALL FROM OUR LORD.
teach.b: But those firmly grounded in knowledge say: we believe in it, it is all from our Lord.

teach.h: DON'T LET OUR HEARTS STRAY, AFTER GUIDANCE.
teach.b: Then verse eight, in Pickthall's translation: "Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us, and bestow upon us mercy from Thy Presence. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Bestower." Look who is praying.
Not beginners. The people the verse calls firm in knowledge, who have studied the hard parts. And look at after Thou hast guided us.
This isn't a prayer to find the way. It's a prayer not to lose it. Guidance, in this verse, isn't a trophy on a shelf.
It can slip. The Prophet's own words make the fit audible: muqallib al-qulub, turner of hearts.
Qalb, heart, and the verb to turn share their letters, as if a heart is the thing that turns. So those who know the hard parts ask, as the Prophet did, to be kept.
This week has been prophets' du'as: Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Ayyub, Yunus, Zakariyya, Sulayman. Today's belongs to everyone who has been guided at all.

how: Some Muslims say 3:8, rabbana la tuzigh qulubana, after the daily prayers or in personal du'a, alongside the Prophet's own prayer, ya muqallib al-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik.

o: the tongue, that speaks a prayer
the soul that leaves the body at death
the heart, the thing that turns

games.q: the believers' du'a — tap the pairs.
p: asked why he said it so often

s: in 3:8 the ones praying are beginners just finding the way
they are those firmly grounded in knowledge, already guided.
the Prophet often asked the turner of hearts to keep his heart firm
Umm Salamah reported it, in al-Tirmidhi.
the du'a asks to be kept after guidance, not only to find it

games.q: you've studied the book for years and know the hard verses well. surah three says what the firmly grounded do next. which is it?
o: pray: don't let our hearts stray.
argue the unclear verses with others.
games.why: they say it's all from our Lord, and then ask not to be turned aside. even the learned pray to be kept.

practice: Find your heartbeat if you can, steady without your help.

If you pray, say the believers' words, in Arabic if you know them or in English: our Lord, don't let our hearts swerve after You have guided us, and give us mercy from You; some Muslims say it after the daily prayer.
If you don't, hold one thing you'd hate to drift from while the heart keeps time.

wordCard.voice: Qalb: heart. It shares its letters with the verb to turn, as if a heart is the very thing that turns, the word behind the Prophet's own prayer to be kept steady. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: our Lord, don't let our hearts swerve (3:8).

carryVoice: Your line: keep my heart. Even the firmly grounded ask to be kept. Until tomorrow.
